purpose: Positive-example (gold standard) corpus. Provides (a) few-shot exemplars for the writer, (b) the reference against which the template was designed, (c) the human baseline in the evaluation.

provenance_rules.public_model: Published by a university writing centre or similar official source as a model email. Citable and legally reusable with attribution. Preferred source class.
provenance_rules.consented_real: An actual student email, collected with written informed consent, anonymised before storage. Requires an ethics note and a consent reference. Never store the original identity.
provenance_rules.synthetic_verified: Generated by a language model, then edited and approved by a human annotator. Must be labelled synthetic wherever it is used. Cannot be counted as evidence of real student practice. Supervisor confirmed on 2026-11-08 that synthetic exemplars are explicitly acceptable as a primary source class, not merely a fallback.
provenance_rules.template_derived: Produced by the app's own template engine. Useful as a baseline condition, never as a gold standard.

annotation_scheme.basis: Move analysis adapted from Swales' genre analysis, combined with e-politeness features from Biesenbach-Lucas (2007). Cite both in the report and state exactly how the scheme was adapted — do not present a borrowed scheme as original.

moves.label: Statement of purpose (why this email exists)
Situation or background, including academic impact
Acknowledgement of the recipient's constraints or the rules
Offer of remedy, evidence, or alternative

annotation_scheme.coding_note: Code moves on the basis of communicative function, not position. A single sentence may realise two moves; record both and say so.

collection_plan.target: 40 to 60 exemplars. Quality of annotation matters more than volume; 40 well-coded exemplars support a credible evaluation, 200 unannotated ones do not.

supervisor_confirmation.statement: The supervisor confirmed that corpus exemplars may be self-authored/synthetic or real cases. Both are acceptable. This explicitly endorses synthetic_verified as a valid primary source class, not merely a fallback when consented_real or public_model exemplars cannot be obtained.
supervisor_confirmation.implication: The collection plan may proceed with a mix of synthetic and real exemplars without requiring all-real data. The provenance separation rule below still applies: synthetic data may serve as input scenarios and as annotated exemplars, but must be labelled wherever it is used.

strata: request type: extension / grade / absence / exam / review
outcome context: before deadline / after deadline / after a decision
collection_plan.ethics: Real student emails are personal data. Collect only with written consent, state the purpose, allow withdrawal before anonymisation, and store anonymised copies only. If consent cannot be obtained within the timeline, synthetic exemplars are explicitly endorsed by the supervisor as an acceptable substitute. Public model emails from university writing centres remain the preferred provenance class where available. Do not scrape a student inbox or a group chat.
where_to_look: University writing centre and EAP course pages that publish model emails to faculty
Published appendices in applied linguistics papers on student-faculty email (check the licence before reusing text)
Your own correspondence, with the recipient's details removed and your own consent as author
Self-authored exemplars written to demonstrate specific move structures and politeness features, labelled as synthetic_verified

exemplars.usable_for: format demonstration only — excluded from evaluation
exemplars.text:
Subject: Extension request — Essay 2, LIN4049

Dear Dr Chan,

I am writing about Essay 2 for LIN4049, which is due on Friday 6 November.

I have been unwell for the past week and have not been able to work at my usual pace. I am sorry to write at short notice.

Would it be possible to have an extension of three days, to Monday 9 November? I understand that any change to the deadline requires your approval, and that a late submission may affect the grade for this assignment.

I can provide supporting documentation if that would be helpful.

Thank you for your time.

Kind regards,
[Your name]
[Student ID]
exemplars.annotation_note: Demonstrates the target shape: one request, dated, mitigated, acknowledges the rule without asserting an outcome, offers evidence conditionally.

exemplars.text:
Subject: Question about feedback — Essay 1, LIN4049

Dear Dr Chan,

I am writing about the feedback on Essay 1 for LIN4049, which I received on 20 October.

I would like to understand the comment on the referencing section, as I had understood the brief to allow the format I used. I am not asking you to change the mark; I would like to make sure I understand the requirement before the next assignment.

Could you clarify which part of the referencing guidance I did not follow, or let me know if it would be better to discuss this in office hours?

Thank you for your time.

Kind regards,
[Your name]
[Student ID]
exemplars.annotation_note: Demonstrates the explicit disclaimer of intent ('I am not asking you to change the mark'), which keeps the email at the 9.2.1 stage and avoids triggering a defensive reading.
